module.definition: A separate structural section of a space station designed for a particular function.

airlock.definition: A chamber with controlled pressure and separate doors that permits passage between different pressure environments.

solar-array.definition: An electrical device made from many connected solar cells that convert sunlight into electricity.
solar-array.exampleUsage: The station’s solar array generated electrical power from sunlight.

docking-port.definition: A connection point on a spacecraft or space station where another spacecraft can attach securely.
docking-port.exampleUsage: The visiting spacecraft approached the docking port slowly.

cupola.definition: A windowed observation module providing views outside the station.

truss.definition: A supporting framework that holds external station equipment such as solar arrays and radiators.

radiator-panel.definition: A panel that releases excess heat from a spacecraft into space.
radiator-panel.exampleUsage: The radiator panel helps control the station's temperature.

antenna.definition: A device that sends or receives radio and television signals.
antenna.exampleUsage: The antenna carried signals for the supported communication system.

hatch.definition: A door or opening in a vehicle, ship, or spacecraft.

spacesuit.definition: A pressure suit worn by astronauts while in outer space.

helmet.definition: A hard covering worn to protect the head.

gloves.definition: Protective hand coverings worn with a spacesuit.

boots.definition: Foot coverings forming part of the astronaut’s clothing or spacesuit in this context.
boots.exampleUsage: The astronaut’s boots formed part of the spacesuit.

tether.definition: A strong line used to keep a person or object attached and secure.

jet-pack.definition: A wearable device that produces thrust to help a person move through the air or, in some space applications, maneuver in microgravity.
jet-pack.exampleUsage: The training display showed an astronaut maneuvering device similar to a jet pack.

tool-belt.definition: A belt worn around the waist keeps hand tools close in pockets and loops. It is useful for carpentry, repairs, and crafts.
tool-belt.exampleUsage: The tool belt kept the worker’s tools close to hand.

visor.definition: A protective transparent or tinted screen on a spacesuit helmet.

oxygen-tank.definition: A strong container used to store oxygen gas for controlled use in equipment or life-support systems.
oxygen-tank.exampleUsage: The life-support system includes monitored oxygen tanks.

communication-headset.definition: A head-worn device with speakers and a microphone for two-way communication.
communication-headset.exampleUsage: The astronaut used a communication headset during the test.

sleeping-pod.definition: A small enclosed or partly enclosed space designed for one person to sleep in.
sleeping-pod.exampleUsage: Each crew member has a compact sleeping pod.

galley.definition: The station area used for food storage and preparation.

exercise-machine.definition: A piece of equipment designed for physical exercise or fitness training.
exercise-machine.exampleUsage: Crew members use an exercise machine to help maintain fitness in microgravity.

toilet.definition: A bathroom fixture used for getting rid of waste from the body.

shower-bag.definition: A bag used to contain supplies or washing material in a specified spacecraft hygiene arrangement; it does not imply an Earth-style shower on the ISS.

velcro-strip.definition: A fastener used to fasten clothing or bags.

book.definition: A set of printed pages bound together for reading.

photo.definition: A picture captured with a camera for a record, report, or memory.

personal-locker.definition: A storage compartment for a crew member's personal belongings.

microscope.definition: Magnifier of the image of small objects.

centrifuge.definition: An apparatus that uses centrifugal force to separate particles from a suspension.

glove-box.definition: A sealed chamber with built-in gloves for handling experiments safely.

plant-growth-chamber.definition: An enclosed space with controlled conditions for growing plants.

water-recycler.definition: A device that recycles water from waste streams.
water-recycler.exampleUsage: The water recycler recovered water through the station’s treatment system.

air-filter.definition: A component that removes specified particles or contaminants from circulating air.

spectrometer.definition: An instrument that measures a spectrum to investigate properties of a sample or radiation.

sample-container.definition: Describes equipment or materials intended to hold a sample for examination in science or home science.

data-logger.definition: An electronic device automatically records and saves measurements from sensors over time, allowing people to study and track changes later.
data-logger.exampleUsage: The data logger saved measurements from the experiment over time.

experiment-rack.definition: A frame or cabinet that holds scientific experiment equipment.

control-panel.definition: A flat section of a device holds the buttons, switches, and dials that control its operation.
control-panel.exampleUsage: The control panel contained the system’s switches and controls.

monitor.definition: A screen that displays information from a computer or instrument.
monitor.exampleUsage: The monitor displayed the file that the technician had opened.

keyboard.definition: Device consisting of a set of keys on a piano or organ or typewriter or typesetting machine or computer or the like.
keyboard.exampleUsage: She entered the sample number using the keyboard.

joystick.definition: A movable control stick used to operate equipment.

radio.definition: A device for communication using radio waves.

map-display.definition: A screen showing a map for reference or navigation.

camera.definition: Equipment for taking photographs (usually consisting of a lightproof box with a lens at one end and light-sensitive film at the other).

alarm.definition: A signal or device warning the crew of a possible problem.

checklist.definition: A list of items (names or tasks etc.) to be checked or consulted.

earth-view.definition: A view of Earth from space.

stars.definition: Luminous astronomical bodies that produce energy through processes including nuclear fusion.

moon.definition: The natural satellite of the Earth.

sun.definition: The star that is the source of light and heat for the planets in the solar system.

satellite.definition: A machine sent into space to collect information and send it back.
satellite.exampleUsage: The artificial satellite followed its orbit around Earth.

space-debris.definition: Human-made objects or fragments in space that are no longer in use.

robotic-arm.definition: A mechanical arm used to move or handle objects.

solar-flare.definition: A sudden intense release of electromagnetic radiation from the Sun associated with magnetic activity.

aurora.definition: An atmospheric phenomenon consisting of bands of light caused by charged solar particles following the earth's magnetic lines of force.

lab-module.definition: A section of the space station containing facilities for scientific experiments.

crew-quarters.definition: The areas where crew members sleep and keep personal belongings.

node.definition: A connecting module joining other station sections and providing access between them.

jetpack.definition: A device worn on the back that produces thrust to move a person.

treadmill.definition: An exercise device consisting of an endless belt on which a person can walk or jog without changing place.
treadmill.exampleUsage: The astronaut used the station treadmill with its required restraint system.

oxygen-generator.definition: Equipment that produces oxygen for the crew to breathe.

comm-dish.definition: A dish-shaped antenna used to send or receive communications.

viewport.definition: A window through which people can see outside a spacecraft.

spacewalk.definition: An activity in which an astronaut works outside a spacecraft while wearing the required protective suit.

experiment.definition: A planned investigation used to test an idea or study a phenomenon.

dock.definition: To connect a spacecraft securely to a compatible spacecraft or station interface.

orbit.definition: The curved path one object follows around another in space.

float.arabicTranslation: يطفو في حالة انعدام الوزن الظاهري
float.definition: To remain suspended or drift in the station without standing on a floor.

exercise.definition: To perform planned physical activity to maintain fitness in this verb list.

repair.definition: To fix something damaged or not working in this verb list.

communicate.definition: To share information or ideas with someone.

window.definition: An opening fitted with transparent material to admit light or provide a view.

laptop.definition: A portable computer with a built-in screen and keyboard.

clock.definition: A device that shows or measures time.
